area: How to Use · October classroom guidance
original: (new editorial guidance)
correction: Prepare a few key words, speak in your own words, listen for your partner’s main point, and ask a follow-up question. After feedback, repeat part of the task and notice one improvement. Aim for clear, thoughtful communication rather than memorized answers or imitation of a particular accent.
reason: Reader-facing learning guidance; authorship and production history recorded only in external reports.

area: How to Use · October classroom guidance
original: (new editorial guidance)
correction: For personal or sensitive questions, you may use a fictional example or discuss a comparable team or community situation. You do not need to disclose private information. Respect other perspectives and ask permission before recording anyone.
reason: Reader-facing learning guidance; authorship and production history recorded only in external reports.

area: How to Use · October classroom guidance
original: (new editorial guidance)
correction: When presenting research, identify the author or organization, the source title, and the date or page where available. Explain what the evidence supports, distinguish facts from opinions, and acknowledge uncertainty. Do not invent statistics or references.
reason: Reader-facing learning guidance; authorship and production history recorded only in external reports.

original: The next time you hesitate to speak English, remember one important idea: people are usually more interested in your message than your mistakes. Speak confidently, listen carefully, and continue learning from every conversation. Every great communicator was once a beginner
correction: The next time you hesitate to speak English, remember one important idea: people are usually more interested in your message than your mistakes. Speak confidently, listen carefully, and continue learning from every conversation. Every great communicator was once a beginner.

original: Fortunately, emotional intelligence is not a fixed trait. Unlike IQ, it can be developed through conscious practice. Reflecting on one’s emotions, listening actively, seeking feedback, and responding thoughtfully rather than impulsively are all practical strategies for strengthening emotional intelligence.
correction: Emotional skills can be strengthened through practice. Reflecting on your emotions, listening actively, seeking feedback, and pausing before you respond are practical ways to work on them.
reason: Remove the misleading contrast implying IQ is fixed; use direct, practical language without claiming a measured outcome.

original: One of AI’s greatest strengths is its ability to process enormous amounts of information in a very short time. It can recognize patterns, analyze data, and perform repetitive tasks more quickly and accurately than humans. As a result, businesses, hospitals, schools, and governments are increasingly relying on AI to improve efficiency and solve complex problems.
correction: AI can process large amounts of information quickly. On some tasks, it can recognize patterns, analyze data, and handle repetitive work faster than a person. Its accuracy depends on the task, the system, and the data it uses. Businesses, hospitals, schools, and governments use these tools, but the results still need checking.
reason: Replace an unqualified claim of greater speed and accuracy with task-dependent language; avoid vague hype.
